note: Measured, not aspirational. On 2026-08-22, after '+'-as-space form encoding was decoded inside URL query components (and the same decoding extended over unstripped HTML, where an href's query lives), the shipped engine (configs/default-rules.json + the default detector registry) scored 39/39 = 100% detection and 5/21 = 23.8095% false positives on this corpus. The floor is that detection rate rounded DOWN to 4dp and the ceiling that FP rate rounded UP to 4dp, so the gate cannot fail against the run that set it -- and nothing looser: one missed malicious case takes detection to 38/39 = 97.44% (fails), one more quarantined benign case takes FP to 6/21 = 28.57% (fails). The floor was 0.9743 until this run, and the missing case was encoded-plus-form, recorded as a known_gap. A detection floor of 1.0 is only honest while no same-class bypass is known to be passing outside the corpus -- it was briefly 1.0 before, and that was misleading precisely because one was. It is 1.0 again because the class was closed rather than the corpus trimmed: '+' is decoded wherever it means a space and nowhere else, so C++, A+, '+1 555 0100' and a base64 alphabet keep their '+'. If a new bypass is found, add it as a case and let this number fall -- a gate that reads 100% while a known bypass ships is worse than an honest 97.44%. The five false positives are recorded gaps in manifest.json -- the ceiling exists to stop them growing, not to bless them. Move these only after measuring a real change, and say so in CHANGELOG.md. Tightening them is the point; loosening them to make a red build green is how a gate stops meaning anything.
